Hi Santiago / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the performance questions you raised:

1) Goals you stated on the call:
- p95 end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> model -> response) target: <= 220ms for single-shot text generation (avg payload ~1.2KB)
- p99 target: <= 400ms
- Sustained throughput requirement: ~120 requests/sec during trading hours (burst to 300 req/s)
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent streams for streaming responses (live market commentary use case)

2) What we committed to provide:
- A short technical note with our hosted API p95/p99 numbers for comparable model families and typical sequence lengths (attached).
- Clarifying questions about how you measure end-to-end latency today (client network vs provider network vs model inference) so we compare apples-to-apples.
- Proposal for a 2-week pilot (test tokens + load plan + mutual action plan) if the numbers look promising.

3) Action items / owners:
- Marissa: Send the perf summary and MAP (attached) + propose pilot timeline (today) 
- Laura: Follow up with specific questions on payloads, streaming chunk sizes, and KV cache behavior.
- Santiago / Priya: Share your current provider observed p95/p99 numbers, and any existing load-test reports or dashboards.

Let me know if I missed anything. If that looks right, I'll loop Legal for the MAP and propose dates for the pilot.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - follow-up

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple of clarifications / notes from our side: 

- Our current provider (ProviderX) measured on our production traffic (US-east clients, avg payload ~1.1KB):
  - p95 end-to-end: ~250ms
  - p99 end-to-end: ~460ms
  - Sustained throughput: 130 req/s, bursts to 320 req/s (we've been throttled occasionally)
  - Streaming: we currently use chunked streaming with 256B chunks; we see tail spikes with >150 concurrent streams

- Measurement scope: our reported numbers include client-side RTT to provider edge + provider processing + model inference. We can run a trimmed test that isolates provider-to-model inference if you need that.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you provide p95/p99 numbers for your hosted API under a similar payload and concurrency profile? Specifically interested in end-to-end observed from US-east to your hosted region.
- How does Redwood handle streaming backpressure and partial chunking (do you support small chunk sizes without increasing p99 tail latency)?

We'll try to share our load-test dashboard this afternoon. If Redwood can show material improvement on p99 under streaming concurrency, we're very interested in a pilot.

—Santiago
Head of Platform Engineering | FinLytics
Santiago.Moreno@finlytics.com

Hi Santiago / Priya —

Laura from Solutions Engineering here — following up with the technical details we discussed and a few clarifying questions so we can size an apples-to-apples test: 

1) Please confirm the typical sequence length / tokens per request (you mentioned ~1-1.5KB payload, can you provide avg token count and max tokens used).

2) Streaming specifics:
- What is your typical chunk size (you mentioned 256B) and chunk frequency?
- Are you doing client-side reassembly or do you rely on the provider to stream coherent chunks?

3) Concurrency / connection model:
- Are the ~200 concurrent streams long-lived WebSocket/HTTP2 connections or short-lived HTTP requests that use streaming responses?

4) Tail sensitivity:
- Is p99 measured at the edge (including client network) or from a synthetic probe in US-east? If you can share raw histograms (json/csv) that helps us match workload distribution.

What we'll provide back (attached):
- redwood_perf_p95_p99_summary.pdf: p95/p99 numbers for our hosted API across comparable payloads and models, with notes on measurement methodology.
- A short runbook for the pilot (including expected load script and what we instrument).

Pilot ask: if you can share a 24h window where you can open a controlled load test, we will run an end-to-end comparison (your client -> our hosted endpoint) and provide a full histogram and side-by-side p95/p99.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m tech sync if useful.

Best,
